cases.reason: Named registered-style earn-and-learn electrician apprenticeship with a concrete public application route, stated eligibility, and published costs; matches the training-advancement focus and serves regional work sites reachable from the Mesa service area.
criticalDetails: Four-year paid apprenticeship: work for a participating contractor plus classroom training; classes accompany full-time work.
Published costs: $40 nonrefundable application fee plus $187 monthly during training; costs should be confirmed as current before paying.
Eligibility: 18 by program start, education and algebra requirements or approved alternatives, ID and school records; military service or documented electrical experience may qualify as an exception.
Physical demands noted: ladders, confined spaces, regular 50-pound lifting; applicants are directed to ask about essential job requirements and accommodations.
Apply via 'How to Apply' at https://pejatc.org/how-to-apply/; webservices@pejatc.org for application help or to arrange use of a training-center computer.
Training centers in Phoenix; job sites vary across the program area — applicant must be able to reach regional work sites.
Admission is competitive; applying does not guarantee selection.
openQuestions: What is the current application deadline or open application window?

cases.reason: Named public workforce program (SCSEP) with paid training, defined federal/state eligibility, and DES-listed grantee contacts covering Maricopa County including Mesa; fits both the public-workforce and population-specific focuses.
criticalDetails: Part-time paid community-service training, typically about 20 hours weekly, paid at the highest applicable minimum wage.

Eligibility: Arizona resident 55 or older, unemployed, authorized to work, income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level, and facing a job barrier (e.g., limited English, disability, poor job prospects).
Arizona Job Connection registration is required and staff verify eligibility.
Contacts listed by DES: 602-841-0403 (Maricopa AARP/Easterseals route), AARP 928-395-2261, NICOA 505-292-2001 for Maricopa County.
Temporary training with limited places and possible waiting lists; participation limits apply.
Wages may affect other benefits — applicants are advised to ask before enrolling.
Program page: https://des.az.gov/services/older-adults/senior-community-service-employment-program
openQuestions: Which grantee currently handles Mesa intake, and is there a Mesa-area office or is intake by phone only?
Are places currently open or is there an active waiting list?
What is the maximum participation duration under current rules?

cases.reason: In-area staffing office with a durable public intake route, verified address, hours, phone, and email, free placement, and multiple work types including temp-to-hire; squarely matches the immediate-employment focus and is not a generic job board.
criticalDetails: Free job placement — no fee to job seekers; weekly pay.
Office: 849 N. Dobson Rd., Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201; Monday–Thursday 8 AM–5 PM, Friday 8 AM–3 PM; call before visiting to arrange application help.
Contact: 480-820-3700 or jobs.mesaaz@expresspros.com; online applications must be submitted to the Mesa office — saving an account alone does not send the application.
Work types: warehouse and manufacturing, skilled trades, office and customer service, professional roles; temporary, evaluation-hire and direct-hire depending on openings.
Bring work and education history, references, contact details; work-eligibility documents needed at interview.
Some roles require a skills assessment or a specific license; placement depends on a suitable opening.

Benefits (health, dental, vision, life, disability, retirement, confidential counseling) apply to workers employed by Express and may require minimum hours or weeks; ExpressLearn courses are for Express-employed workers only.
After an assignment ends, the worker must contact the office to be considered for another.
openQuestions: Which work-eligibility documents are required at interview?

cases.reason: Named disability supported-employment provider with Mesa sites and an explicit referral and funding path; matches the supported-employment focus, with the caveat that entry generally runs through a referral source.
criticalDetails: Services: career planning, work preparation, computer skills, job development, supported employment, community work experience, and ongoing support.
Entry and funding depend on program and referral; listed funding routes are VR, DDD, behavioral-health plans, and private pay.
Contact: 480-969-3800 (Copa main office) and ask for Employment Related Services; referrals sent to referrals@copahealth.org.
People with a case manager, DDD support coordinator, or VR counselor should ask that person about a referral.
Main office 924 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa; employment services listed at two Mesa sites plus other Valley locations — call for the correct employment site before traveling.
Transportation is offered to community group work sites; getting to intake or training must be asked about separately.
The provider's description of what businesses pay Copa does not establish a participant wage; facility training, group work experience, and competitive job support are different services.
Program page: https://copahealth.org/copa-employment-related-services/
openQuestions: Can someone without an existing case manager or VR counselor self-refer, and what is that path?

cases.reason: Free, named nine-week vocational training with published screening rules, a clear application path, and forklift/culinary skill outcomes; usable from Mesa but requires a daily commute to west Phoenix and full weekday availability, which should be surfaced up front.
criticalDetails: Two tracks: Community Kitchen (culinary) and LIFT (logistics, inventory, forklift); training is free.
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7 AM–3 PM for nine weeks at 3003 W. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85017 — a substantial daily trip from Mesa.
Eligibility: 18+, authorized to work, facing employment barriers, ready for steady work, consistent attendance required.
Housing requirement: must live in a shelter, own or rented home, or a halfway house; other arrangements require asking staff.
Background and drug screening apply, including random drug tests; arson and registered-sex-offender exclusions are published.
Apply by calling 602-343-3183, applying online, dropping off an application, or faxing to 480-780-3799; staff arrange an interview and issue an accepted, waitlisted, or declined decision.
Housing is not included and employment is not guaranteed.
Program page: https://www.firstfoodbank.org/learn/programs/community-kitchen/

criticalDetails: Neighborhood Brigade paid cleanup work is restricted to residents of Ozanam Manor and the Washington Street housing programs.
Rosalie's Place offers workforce housing with employment and money-management support for adults working or seeking work; staff screen applicants.

Unresolved cost conflict: the Rosalie's workforce page describes free housing with 60% of net income saved, while the general intake page states residents with income pay 30% — the applicable rule must be confirmed before agreeing.
Housing screening: 602-850-6900, 8 AM–3 PM; phone screening followed by an in-person interview. Rosalie's Place questions: 602-261-6870, Monday–Friday 8 AM–3 PM.
Washington Street shelter requires a partner referral and does not accept walk-ups.
Locations: Rosalie's Place and Ozanam Manor at 320 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003; Washington Street shelter at 2739 E. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85034.
Mesa Dining Room, 49 W. Broadway Rd., is listed among work-readiness locations, and 602-619-9411 is given — but whether job help is actually offered there, and on what schedule, is unverified.
Beds and paid crew openings are limited.
